You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A (Issuer), together with Verizon ABS LLC (Depositor); counterparty is Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless (as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

{"sectionRef":"§ II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0031","text":"ARTICLE II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES"},{"id":"p0032","text":"Section 2.1 Transfers of Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0033","text":"(a) Transfer and Absolute Assignment of Initial Receivables. In consideration of the Issuer's delivery to the Depositor of the Notes, the Class A Certificate and the Class B Certificate, effective on the Closing Date, the Depositor transfers and absolutely assigns to the Issuer, without recourse (other than the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement), all of the Depositor's right, title and interest, whether now owned or later acquired, in the Initial Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property. The Depositor certifies that the Credit Enhancement Test and the Pool Composition Tests are satisfied for the transfer and assignment of the Initial Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property on the Closing Date."},{"id":"p0034","text":"(b) Transfers and Absolute Assignments of Additional Receivables. Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions in Section 2.1(d), effective on each Acquisition Date, in consideration of the Issuer's distribution to the Depositor of the (i) Additional Receivables Cash"},{"id":"p0035","text":"Transfer Amount for the Additional Receivables to be transferred to the Issuer on that Acquisition Date and (ii) an increase in the Class B Certificate Principal Balance in an amount equal to the excess, if any, of the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount over the Additional Receivables Cash Transfer Amount for such Additional Receivables, the Depositor will transfer and absolutely assign to the Issuer, without recourse (other than the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement), all of the Depositor's right, title and interest, whether then owned or later acquired, in the Additional Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0036","text":"(c) No Assumption of Obligations. These transfers and absolute assignments do not, and are not intended to, include any obligation of the Depositor or any Originator to the Obligors or any other Person relating to the Receivables and the other Depositor Transferred Property, and the Issuer does not assume any of these obligations."},{"id":"p0037","text":"(d) Conditions for Transfers of Additional Receivables. The transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property on each Acquisition Date will be subject to the satisfaction of the following conditions on or before such Acquisition Date:"},{"id":"p0038","text":"(i) Transfer Notice. At least two (2) Business Days before the applicable Acquisition Date, the Administrator shall deliver to the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee a Transfer Notice for the Additional Receivables to be transferred and absolutely assigned on that Acquisition Date, which will specify the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount and attach or include therewith the Schedule of Receivables;"},{"id":"p0039","text":"(ii) Satisfaction of Tests. After giving effect to the transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables by the Depositor to the Issuer, (A) the Credit Enhancement Test is satisfied and (B) the Receivables, in the aggregate, owned by the Issuer, excluding any Temporarily Excluded Receivables, satisfy each of the Pool Composition Tests under Section 3.5(b); and"},{"id":"p0040","text":"(iii) Depositor's Certifications. The Depositor certifies that:"},{"id":"p0041","text":"(A) as of such Acquisition Date, (1) the Depositor is Solvent and will not become insolvent as a result of the transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables on the Acquisition Date, (2) the Depositor does not intend to incur or believe that it would incur debts that would be beyond the Depositor's ability to pay as they matured and (3) the transfer and assignment of the Additional Receivables is not made by the Depositor with actual intent to hinder, delay or defraud any Person;"},{"id":"p0042","text":"(B) each of the representations and warranties made by the Depositor under Sections 2.4(a) and 2.4(b), in each case, solely with respect to the related Additional Receivables, will be true and correct as of the Acquisition Date; and"},{"id":"p0043","text":"(C) all conditions to the transfer and assignment of the related Additional Receivables by the Originators to the Depositor under"},{"id":"p0044","text":"2"},{"id":"p0045","text":"Section 2.1(d) of the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement and by the Master Trust to the Depositor under Section 2.1(d) of the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement, as applicable, have been satisfied."},{"id":"p0046","text":"The delivery by the Administrator, on behalf of the Depositor, of the Transfer Notice will be considered a certification by the Depositor that the conditions set forth in this Section 2.1(d) have been satisfied or will be satisfied on the Acquisition Date."},{"id":"p0047","text":"Section 2.2 Acknowledgement of Further Assignments. The Depositor acknowledges that, under the Indenture, the Issuer will assign and pledge the Depositor Transferred Property and related property and rights to the Indenture Trustee for the benefit of the Secured Parties."},{"id":"p0048","text":"Section 2.3 Savings Clause. The Depositor and the Issuer intend that each transfer and assignment under this Agreement be an absolute transfer and assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property, conveying good title to the Depositor Transferred Property free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens, from the Depositor to the Issuer. The Depositor and the Issuer intend that the Depositor Transferred Property not be a part of the Depositor's estate if there is a bankruptcy or insolvency of the Depositor. If, despite the intent of the Depositor and the Issuer, a transfer and assignment of Depositor Transferred Property under this Agreement is determined to be a pledge for a financing or is determined not to be an absolute transfer and assignment, the Depositor Grants to the Issuer a security interest in the Depositor's right, title and interest in the Depositor Transferred Property to secure a loan in an amount equal to all amounts payable by the Depositor under this Agreement, all amounts payable as principal of or interest on the Notes, all amounts payable as Servicing Fees under this Agreement and all other amounts payable by the Issuer under the Transaction Documents. In that case, this Agreement will be a security agreement under Law and the Issuer will have the rights and remedies of a secured party and creditor under the UCC."},{"id":"p0049","text":"Section 2.4 Representations and Warranties About Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0050","text":"(a) Representations and Warranties About Pool of Receivables. The Depositor makes the following representations and warranties about the pool of Receivables on which the Issuer is relying in acquiring the Depositor Transferred Property. The representations and warranties are made as of the Closing Date (for the Initial Receivables) and as of each Acquisition Date (for the related Additional Receivables) and will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement and the pledge of the Depositor Transferred Property by the Issuer to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture."},{"id":"p0051","text":"(i) Valid Transfer and Assignment. This Agreement evidences a valid transfer and absolute assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property from the Depositor to the Issuer, enforceable against creditors of, purchasers from and transferees and absolute assignees of the Depositor."},{"id":"p0052","text":"(ii) Good Title to Depositor Transferred Property. Immediately before the transfer and absolute assignment under this Agreement, the Depositor has good title to"},{"id":"p0053","text":"3"},{"id":"p0054","text":"the Depositor Transferred Property free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens, and, immediately after the transfer and absolute assignment under this Agreement, the Issuer will have good title to the Depositor Transferred Property, free and clear of any Lien, other than Permitted Liens."},{"id":"p0055","text":"(iii) Security Interest in Depositor Transferred Property."},{"id":"p0056","text":"(A) This Agreement creates a valid and continuing security interest (as defined in the applicable UCC) in the Depositor Transferred Property in favor of the Issuer, which is prior to any Lien, other than Permitted Liens, and is enforceable against all creditors of, purchasers from and transferees and absolute assignees of the Depositor."},{"id":"p0057","text":"(B) All filings (including UCC filings) necessary in any jurisdiction to give the Depositor a first priority, validly perfected ownership and security interest in the Originator Transferred Property and the Master Trust Transferred Property, to give the Issuer a first priority, validly perfected ownership and security interest in the Depositor Transferred Property and to give the Indenture Trustee a first priority perfected security interest in the Collateral, will be made within ten (10) days after the Closing Date or the related Acquisition Date, as applicable."},{"id":"p0058","text":"(C) All financing statements filed or to be filed against the Depositor in favor of the Issuer describing the Depositor Transferred Property transferred under this Agreement will contain a statement to the following effect: \"A purchase, absolute assignment or transfer of or security interest in any collateral described in this financing statement will violate the rights of the Secured Party/Assignee.\""},{"id":"p0059","text":"(D) The Depositor has not authorized the filing of and is not aware of any financing statements against the Depositor that include a description of collateral covering any Depositor Transferred Property other than the financing statements relating to the security interest Granted to the Depositor under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement or by the Issuer to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture, or that has been terminated."},{"id":"p0060","text":"(b) Representations and Warranties About Security Interest. If the transfer and absolute assignment of the Depositor Transferred Property under this Agreement is determined to be a pledge relating to a financing or is determined not to be a transfer and absolute assignment, the Depositor makes the following representations and warranties on which the Issuer is relying in acquiring the Depositor Transferred Property, which representations and warranties are made as of the Closing Date or as of the related Acquisition Date, as applicable,"},{"id":"p0061","text":"4"},{"id":"p0062","text":"will survive termination of this Agreement and may not be waived by the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee:"},{"id":"p0063","text":"(i) Valid Security Interest. This Agreement creates a valid and continuing security interest (as defined in the applicable UCC) in the Depositor Transferred Property in favor of the Issuer, which is prior to all other Liens, other than Permitted Liens, and is enforceable against creditors of, purchasers from and transferees and absolute assignees of the Depositor."},{"id":"p0064","text":"(ii) Type. Each Receivable is (A) if the Receivable is not secured by the related Device, an \"account\" or \"payment intangible,\" or (B) if the Receivable is secured by the related Device, \"chattel paper,\" in each case, within the meaning of the applicable UCC."},{"id":"p0065","text":"(iii) Good Title. Immediately before the transfer and absolute assignment under this Agreement, the Depositor owns and has good title to the Depositor Transferred Property free and clear of all Liens, other than Permitted Liens. The Depositor has received all consents and approvals required by the terms of the Depositor Transferred Property to Grant to the Issuer its right, title and interest in the Depositor Transferred Property, except to the extent the requirement for consent or approval is extinguished under the applicable UCC."},{"id":"p0066","text":"(iv) Filing Financing Statements. The Depositor has caused, or will cause within ten (10) days after the Closing Date, the filing of all appropriate financing statements in the proper filing office in the appropriate jurisdictions under applicable Law to perfect the security interest Granted in the Depositor Transferred Property to the Issuer under this Agreement. All financing statements filed or to be filed against the Depositor in favor of the Issuer under this Agreement describing the Depositor Transferred Property will contain a statement to the following effect: \"A purchase, absolute assignment or transfer of or grant of a security interest in any collateral described in this financing statement will violate the rights of the Secured Parties.\""},{"id":"p0067","text":"(v) No Other Transfer, Grant or Financing Statement. Other than the security interest Granted to the Issuer under this Agreement, the Depositor has not transferred or Granted a security interest in any of the Depositor Transferred Property. The Depositor has not authorized the filing of and is not aware of any financing statements against the Depositor that include a description of collateral covering any of the Depositor Transferred Property, other than financing statements relating to the security interest Granted to the Issuer. The Depositor is not aware of any judgment or tax Lien filings against it."},{"id":"p0068","text":"Section 2.5 Originators' Reacquisition and Servicer's Acquisition of Receivables for Breach of Representations."},{"id":"p0069","text":"(a) Representations and Warranties from Receivables Transfer Agreements. Each Originator and the Servicer, severally has made, as of the Closing Date, and each Originator or the Servicer, as applicable, severally will make, as of each Acquisition Date, the Eligibility"},{"id":"p0070","text":"5"},{"id":"p0071","text":"Representation about the Receivables transferred and absolutely assigned by such Originator or the Master Trust, respectively, on that date, and has consented to the transfer by the Depositor to the Issuer of the Depositor's rights to such Eligibility Representation. The Issuer is relying on each applicable Originator's or the Servicer's Eligibility Representation in acquiring the Receivables, which Eligibility Representation will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Receivables by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement and the pledge of the Receivables to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture."},{"id":"p0072","text":"(b) Reacquisition or Acquisition. Under Section 2.1(a), the Depositor has transferred and absolutely assigned to the Issuer the Depositor's rights under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, including the right to require (i) an Originator to reacquire any Receivables transferred and absolutely assigned by it under the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement or (ii) the Servicer to acquire any Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by the Master Trust under the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement, in each case, for which such party has made the Eligibility Representation if, in each case, there is a breach of such Eligibility Representation, such breach is not cured and such breach results in a material adverse effect on the Issuer. If any Originator or the Servicer breaches the Eligibility Representation made by it with respect to any Receivable transferred by such Originator or the Master Trust, respectively, to the Depositor, such breach is not cured and such breach has a material adverse effect on the Issuer, then the Depositor will enforce such Originator's or the Servicer's obligation, as applicable, to reacquire or acquire, respectively, any such Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by it to the Depositor for which the Eligibility Representation was breached pursuant to Section 3.4 of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."},{"id":"p0073","text":"(c) Reacquisition or Acquisition Sole Remedy. The sole remedy of the Depositor, the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee for a breach of any Eligibility Representation is to require the related Originator or the Servicer, as applicable, to reacquire or acquire, respectively, the Receivable under Section 3.4 of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."},{"id":"p0074","text":"Section 2.6 Originators' Reacquisition or Servicer's Acquisition of Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivables."},{"id":"p0075","text":"(a) Reacquisition or Acquisition. Under Section 2.1(a), the Depositor has transferred and absolutely assigned to the Issuer the Depositor's rights under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, including the right to require (i) an Originator to reacquire any Receivables transferred and absolutely assigned by it under the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement or (ii) the Servicer to acquire any Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by the Master Trust under the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement, in each case, when such Receivable becomes a Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable. If any Receivable becomes a Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable, the Depositor will enforce such Originator's or the Servicer's obligation, as applicable, to reacquire or acquire, respectively, any such Receivable transferred and absolutely assigned by it to the Depositor pursuant to Section 4.6 or 4.7, respectively, of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."},{"id":"p0076","text":"(b) Reacquisition or Acquisition Sole Remedy. If a Receivable becomes a Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable, the sole remedy of the Depositor, the Issuer or the Indenture Trustee is to require the related Originator or the Servicer, as applicable, to reacquire"},{"id":"p0077","text":"6"},{"id":"p0078","text":"or acquire, respectively, the Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivable under Section 4.6 or 4.7, respectively, of the applicable Receivables Transfer Agreement."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0349","text":"ARTICLE VIII TERMINATION"},{"id":"p0350","text":"Section 8.1 Optional Acquisition of Receivables; Clean-Up Redemption of Notes."},{"id":"p0351","text":"(a) Optional Acquisition. On each Payment Date following the last day of a Collection Period as of which the aggregate Principal Balance of the Receivables shall be equal to or less than 10% of the aggregate Principal Balance of the Receivables as of the Closing Date, the Class A Certificateholder (for as long as the Class A Certificateholder is an Originator or an Affiliate of the Originators), with the consent of the Administrator, on behalf of the Issuer, shall have the option to acquire, as of the end of the immediately preceding Collection Period, any Receivables remaining in the Trust Property on such date by transferring to the Issuer an amount equal to the Optional Acquisition Amount (the \"Optional Acquisition\"), and to redeem the Notes, in whole but not in part (the \"Clean-Up Redemption\") without any Make-Whole Payment (other than any Make-Whole Payments already due and payable on such date)."},{"id":"p0352","text":"(b) Exercise of Optional Acquisition and Clean-Up Redemption of Notes. The Class A Certificateholder may exercise its option set forth in Section 8.1(a) by notifying the Issuer, the Servicer, the Indenture Trustee, the Owner Trustee and the Rating Agencies, in writing, at least ten (10) days before the Payment Date on which the Optional Acquisition is to be exercised,"},{"id":"p0353","text":"37"},{"id":"p0354","text":"After receiving such notice, the Indenture Trustee will promptly notify the Noteholders of the resulting Clean-Up Redemption and provide instructions for surrender of the Notes for final payment including all accrued and unpaid interest and any applicable Make-Whole Payments already due and payable on the Notes, as set forth in Section 10.1(a) of the Indenture."},{"id":"p0355","text":"On the Payment Date related to the Collection Period in which the Optional Acquisition is exercised, the Class A Certificateholder will deposit into the Collection Account the acquisition amount for such remaining Receivables as set forth in Section 8.1(a) equal to the fair market value of such Receivables as of the last day of the Collection Period immediately preceding such Payment Date as agreed upon by the Class A Certificateholder and the Issuer (the \"Optional Acquisition Amount\"); provided that the transfer may only occur if the Optional Acquisition Amount, together with any amounts on deposit in the Bank Accounts, is greater than or equal to the sum of (A) the Note Balance of the Notes, any accrued but unpaid interest and any unpaid Make-Whole Payments and (B) all other amounts payable by the Issuer under the Transaction Documents including, but not limited to, all fees, expenses and indemnities owed to the Indenture Trustee and the Owner Trustee under the Transaction Documents as of such date."},{"id":"p0356","text":"For the avoidance of doubt, if the Class A Certificateholder and the Issuer cannot agree on the Optional Acquisition Amount, the Class A Certificateholder will not be permitted to exercise its option set forth in Section 8.1(a). On the Payment Date on which the Optional Acquisition is to be exercised, the Indenture Trustee shall transfer any amounts on deposit in the Reserve Account, the Acquisition Account and the Negative Carry Account into the Collection Account. Upon the exercise of the Optional Acquisition, the Notes will be redeemed and paid in full."},{"id":"p0357","text":"Section 8.2 Optional Redemption of Notes."},{"id":"p0358","text":"(a) Optional Redemption. On any Payment Date on and after the Payment Date in February 2021, the Class A Certificateholder (for as long as the Class A Certificateholder is an Originator or an Affiliate of the Originators), with the consent of the Administrator, on behalf of the Issuer, shall have the option to redeem the Notes, in whole but not in part (the \"Optional Redemption\"), with a required Make-Whole Payment."},{"id":"p0359","text":"(b) Exercise of Optional Redemption. The Class A Certificateholder may exercise its option set forth in Section 8.2(a) by notifying the Issuer, the Servicer, the Indenture Trustee, the Owner Trustee and the Rating Agencies, in writing, at least ten (10) days before the Payment Date on which the Optional Redemption is to be exercised. After receiving such notice, the Indenture Trustee will promptly notify the Noteholders of the Optional Redemption and provide instructions for surrender of the Notes for final payment including all accrued and unpaid interest and any applicable Make-Whole Payments due and payable on the Notes, as set forth in Section 10.1(a) of the Indenture."},{"id":"p0360","text":"On the Payment Date on which the Optional Redemption is to be exercised, the Issuer shall transfer the entire pool of Receivables to another Verizon special purpose entity or a third-party purchaser and the party receiving the Receivables shall cause the acquisition amount received by the Issuer for the Receivables to be deposited by the Issuer (or the Servicer, on its behalf) into the Collection Account, which amount shall be equal to the fair market value of such Receivables as of the last day of the Collection Period immediately preceding such Payment Date as agreed upon by the Class A Certificateholder and the Issuer; provided that the transfer"},{"id":"p0361","text":"38"},{"id":"p0362","text":"may only occur if the amount received in connection with any such transfer, together with any amounts on deposit in the Bank Accounts, is greater than or equal to the sum of (A) the Note Balance of the Notes, any accrued but unpaid interest and any unpaid Make-Whole Payments and (B) all other amounts payable by the Issuer under the Transaction Documents including, but not limited to, all fees, expenses and indemnities owed to the Indenture Trustee and the Owner Trustee under the Transaction Documents as of such date. On the Payment Date on which the Optional Redemption is to be exercised, the Indenture Trustee shall transfer any amounts on deposit in the Reserve Account, the Acquisition Account and the Negative Carry Account into the Collection Account. **Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

MINCOMMIT is satisfied at the **preferred** position — the Transfer and Servicing Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on the Issuer or Depositor.

Key points from the review:

- **Additional Receivables (Art. II)** — Section 2.1(b)–(d) transfers are *conditional* (Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests, Depositor certifications), and consideration equals the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount for receivables actually transferred. Nothing obliges the Issuer to acquire any minimum volume.
- **Acquisition / Negative Carry Account funding (Art. IV)** — Section 4.4(d)(i) and 4.4(c)(i) deposits are made by the Class A Certificateholder "solely at its option." The Required Acquisition Deposit Amount and Required Negative Carry Amount are internal cash-trapping levels, with excesses released to Certificateholders — not payments we owe the counterparty.
- **Article VIII** — Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption are options exercisable by the Class A Certificateholder, conditioned on full payment of the Notes; no obligation on us.
- **Direction check** — the only "shortfall" mechanic (Section 4.3(h) Credit Payments) runs *to* us: the Marketing Agent must fund shortfalls caused by Obligor Credits. Not flagged.
- **Noted, not flagged** — the $425,000 Additional Successor Servicer Fee floor is a servicing-transition fee for a replacement servicer, which supports our right to replace Cellco rather than restricting us.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on the Issuer or Depositor, so it sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; consideration is paid only for property actually transferred). The closest analogues all cut in our favour or are purely optional: (i) transfers of Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b)-(d) are conditional (Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests, Depositor certifications) and consideration equals the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount for receivables actually acquired — the Issuer is nowhere obliged to acquire a minimum volume; (ii) funding of the Acquisition Account and the related Negative Carry Account under Section 4.4(d)(i) and 4.4(c)(i) is made by the Class A Certificateholder "solely at its option", and Required Acquisition Deposit Amount / Required Negative Carry Amount are only internal cash-trapping levels with excesses released back to the Certificateholders, not payments we must make to the counterparty; (iii) the Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Article VIII are options, not obligations, and require full payment of the Notes; and (iv) the only "shortfall" mechanic (Section 4.3(h) Credit Payments) is an obligation of the Marketing Agent to fund us. The $425,000 Additional Successor Servicer Fee floor is a servicing-transition fee for a replacement servicer, not a purchase commitment, and it supports our ability to replace Cellco. No redline required.

Issuer: TRANSFER AND SERVICING AGREEMENT, dated as of January 29, 2020 (this "Agreement"), among VERIZON OWNER TRUST 2020-A, a Delaware statutory trust, as issuer (the "Issuer"), VERIZON ABS LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as depositor (the "Depositor"), and Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless, a Delaware general partnership ("Cellco"), as servicer (in such capacity, the "Servicer"), as marketing agent (in such capacity, the "Marketing Agent") and as custodian (in such capacity, the "Custodian").
Depositor: TRANSFER AND SERVICING AGREEMENT, dated as of January 29, 2020 (this "Agreement"), among VERIZON OWNER TRUST 2020-A, a Delaware statutory trust, as issuer (the "Issuer"), VERIZON ABS LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as depositor (the "Depositor"), and Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless, a Delaware general partnership ("Cellco"), as servicer (in such capacity, the "Servicer"), as marketing agent (in such capacity, the "Marketing Agent") and as custodian (in such capacity, the "Custodian").
Optional Acquisition: (a) Optional Acquisition. On each Payment Date following the last day of a Collection Period as of which the aggregate Principal Balance of the Receivables shall be equal to or less than 10% of the aggregate Principal Balance of the Receivables as of the Closing Date, the Class A Certificateholder (for as long as the Class A Certificateholder is an Originator or an Affiliate of the Originators), with the consent of the Administrator, on behalf of the Issuer, shall have the option to acquire, as of the end of the immediately preceding Collection Period, any Receivables remaining in the Trust Property on such date by transferring to the Issuer an amount equal to the Optional Acquisition Amount (the "Optional Acquisition"), and to redeem the Notes, in whole but not in part (the "Clean-Up Redemption") without any Make-Whole Payment (other than any Make-Whole Payments already due and payable on such date).
Optional Acquisition Amount: On the Payment Date related to the Collection Period in which the Optional Acquisition is exercised, the Class A Certificateholder will deposit into the Collection Account the acquisition amount for such remaining Receivables as set forth in Section 8.1(a) equal to the fair market value of such Receivables as of the last day of the Collection Period immediately preceding such Payment Date as agreed upon by the Class A Certificateholder and the Issuer (the "Optional Acquisition Amount"); provided that the transfer may only occur if the Optional Acquisition Amount, together with any amounts on deposit in the Bank Accounts, is greater than or equal to the sum of (A) the Note Balance of the Notes, any accrued but unpaid interest and any unpaid Make-Whole Payments and (B) all other amounts payable by the Issuer under the Transaction Documents including, but not limited to, all fees, expenses and indemnities owed to the Indenture Trustee and the Owner Trustee under the Transaction Documents as of such date.
Acquisition Account: "Acquisition Account" means the subaccount of the Collection Account established under Section 4.1(a) of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement.
Acquisition Amount: "Acquisition Amount" means, for an Acquired Receivable for which the Acquisition Amount is to be included in Available Funds for a Payment Date, the excess of (i) the present value of the Principal Balance of the Receivable as of the last day of the Collection Period immediately preceding the related Collection Period (calculated using the Discount Rate on the basis of a 360-day year of twelve 30-day months and assuming each amount is received at the end of the Collection Period in which the amount is scheduled to be received) over (ii) all cash collections and any other cash proceeds received by the Issuer on the related Receivable from (but excluding) the last day of the Collection Period immediately preceding the related Collection Period to the day on which such Receivable becomes an Acquired Receivable.
Acquisition Date: "Acquisition Date" means each date during the Revolving Period on which the Issuer acquires Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b) of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement and the Depositor acquires Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b) of the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement or Section 2.1(a) of the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement; provided that there shall be no more than five (5) Acquisition Dates in any calendar month.
Additional Receivable: "Additional Receivable" means any device payment plan agreement acquired by the Issuer on an Acquisition Date and listed on the Schedule of Receivables attached to a Transfer Notice delivered to the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee in connection with such Acquisition Date.
Administrator: "Administrator" means Cellco, in its capacity as administrator under the Administration Agreement.
Affiliate: "Affiliate" means, for a specified Person (other than a natural Person), (a) another Person controlling, controlled by or under common control with the specified Person, (b) any other Person beneficially owning or controlling more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities or rights of or interest in the capital, distributions or profits of the specified Person or (c) any controlling shareholder of, or partner in, the specified Person. For the purposes of this definition, "control" when used with respect to any Person means the direct or indirect possession of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of the Person, whether through ownership, by contract, arrangement or understanding, or otherwise.
Business Day: "Business Day" means any day other than (a) a Saturday, Sunday or other day on which banks in New York, New York or any jurisdiction in which the Corporate Trust Office of the Indenture Trustee or the Owner Trustee is located are authorized or required to close or (b) a holiday on the Federal Reserve calendar.
Certificate: "Certificate" means either the Class A Certificate or the Class B Certificate, as the context requires.
Certificateholder: "Certificateholder" means the registered holder of a Certificate.
Class: "Class" means the Class A-1a Notes, the Class A-1b Notes, the Class B Notes and the Class C Notes, as applicable.
Class A Certificate: "Class A Certificate" means the Class A Certificate executed by the Issuer and authenticated by the Owner Trustee, evidencing a portion of the Equity Interest in the Issuer, substantially in the form attached as Exhibit B-1 to the Trust Agreement.
Class A Certificateholder: "Class A Certificateholder" means collectively, the Originators or their designee.
Clean-Up Redemption: "Clean-Up Redemption" has the meaning stated in Section 8.1(a) of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement.
Closing Date: "Closing Date" means January 29, 2020.
Collection Account: "Collection Account" means the account or accounts established under Section 4.1(a) of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement.
Collection Period: "Collection Period" means each calendar month. For a Payment Date, the related Collection Period means (i) for any Payment Date other than the initial Payment Date, the Collection Period immediately preceding the month in which the Payment Date occurs, or (ii) for the initial Payment Date, the period from the end of the calendar day on the Initial Cutoff Date and ending on and including the last day of the month immediately preceding the initial Payment Date. For purposes of determining the Principal Balance, Pool Balance or Note Pool Factor, the related Collection Period is the month in which the Principal Balance, Pool Balance or Note Pool Factor is determined.
Collections: "Collections" means, for a Collection Period, all cash collections received from Obligors and any other cash proceeds (whether in the form of cash, wire transfer or check) in respect of the Receivables received and applied by the Servicer to the payment of the Receivables during that Collection Period, but excluding:
Credit: "Credit" means any payment credit (including one-time upfront credits and contingent, recurring credits), including the application of a returned security deposit, allocated to the account of an Obligor that is applied by the Servicer against amounts due on the Obligor's related invoice.
Credit Payment: "Credit Payment" means, with respect to any Collection Period, an amount equal to the reduction in the amount owed by an Obligor under a Receivable due to the application of any Credits to such Obligor's account that would have otherwise constituted Collections during such Collection Period.
Depositor Transferred Property: "Depositor Transferred Property" means, for the Closing Date and any Acquisition Date, (a) the Originator Transferred Property, (b) the Master Trust Transferred Property, (c) the Depositor's rights under the Receivables Transfer Agreements, (d) all present and future claims,
Grant: "Grant" means to mortgage, pledge, assign and to grant a lien on and a security interest in the relevant property.

Marketing Agent: "Marketing Agent" means Cellco.
Negative Carry Account: "Negative Carry Account" means the account or accounts established under Section 4.1(a) of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement.
Obligor: "Obligor" means the Person that has signed the account agreement of which the device payment plan agreement that constitutes the Receivable is a part and who owes payments under the Receivable.
Originator: "Originator" means (i) with respect to the Initial Receivables or the Additional Receivables, any of Cellco or certain Affiliates of Verizon listed on Schedule B to the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement and (ii) with respect to the Additional Receivables transferred to the Depositor pursuant to the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement, any additional Affiliate of Verizon not listed on Schedule B to the Originator Receivables Transfer Agreement
Payment Date: "Payment Date" means the 20th day of each month or, if not a Business Day, the next Business Day, starting in March 2020. For a Collection Period, the related Payment Date means the Payment Date following the end of the Collection Period.
Principal Balance: "Principal Balance" means, for a Receivable as of the last day of a month, an amount (not less than zero) equal to, without duplication:

Required Negative Carry Amount: "Required Negative Carry Amount" means, for any Payment Date during the Revolving Period, an amount equal to the product of (i) the amount in the Acquisition Account on the Payment Date (after giving effect to all payments under Section 8.2(c) of the Indenture and the acquisition of Additional Receivables, if any, on the Payment Date), (ii) the weighted average Note Interest Rate and (iii) 1/12.

Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-d2bcb466","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"Section 6.3 gives us a counterparty-side indemnity: Cellco, as Servicer (including as Custodian) and as Marketing Agent, indemnifies the Issuer and the trustees and their officers, directors, employees and agents for all claims, actions, suits, damages, liabilities and reasonable legal fees resulting from its willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, with standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery absent prejudice, counterparty-funded defence with counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Person, separate counsel on conflict, and no settlement without consent), plus survival beyond resignation, termination and trustee removal. The indemnity is uncapped, so it is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap, and there is no reverse indemnity from the Issuer or Depositor anywhere in the agreement (Article IX imposes only perfection, expense and non-petition/limited recourse covenants), so the walk-away risk of a one-way customer indemnity is absent. Two minor points we note but do not redline: there is no IP-infringement limb (immaterial here, as this transfer and servicing agreement involves no vendor deliverables, licensed technology or IP grant), and the Depositor is not itself an \"Indemnified Person\" under Section 6.3(a), which is consistent with the transaction structure where the Depositor's recourse runs through the originator/transfer documents.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-1c9a02e8","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"needs_review","rationale":"Worker failed and requires manual review: Tool loop exceeded 12 iterations","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-assign-ad4fd7dd","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"Section 10.2(a) imposes a symmetric consent requirement on our Depositor and on Cellco as Servicer, but expressly carves out Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6. Section 5.3 lets the Depositor's merger/consolidation counterparty, business successor, or an Affiliate assignee become the successor Depositor without consent (notice/officer's certificate and opinions only), which is the affiliate/successor M&A carve-out the playbook requires; Section 7.6 gives Cellco the mirror-image treatment. The Issuer is not restricted at all, and Section 2.2 acknowledges the Issuer's assignment and pledge of the Depositor Transferred Property to the Indenture Trustee for the Secured Parties, so our financing-side transfers are preserved and Section 10.2(b) binds permitted successors and assigns. There is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the document (no \"change of control\" language), and Section 7.1 is a \"No Resignation\" covenant barring Cellco from resigning unless legally unable to perform, so the counterparty has no exit or re-pricing right on our reorganisation — the walk-away scenarios are absent. Two points short of the pure preferred position are noted rather than flagged: the third-party consent gate is not expressed as \"not to be unreasonably withheld\" and there is no competitor bar on a Servicer assignment (both are structural noteholder/rating-agency protections in a securitization and apply symmetrically), and Section 6.4 permits Cellco free delegation while it is Servicer or Custodian — acceptable because no delegation or contracting relieves it of responsibility for those obligations. On its material terms the package sits at or above the fallback (mutual assignment to successors with notice), so we do not redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-d1b2c4f7","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"No exclusivity, \"sole supplier\" or requirements-purchasing covenant binds us (the Issuer or the Depositor) anywhere in the agreement. The only \"exclusive\" references are (i) Section 9.10's notice of exclusive control over the Cap Collateral Account — a control right that runs in the Issuer's favour — and (ii) the nonexclusive jurisdiction clause in Section 10.6, neither of which is a restrictive covenant. Cellco's appointments as Servicer (Article III), Custodian (Section 3.10) and Marketing Agent (Section 3.11) are ordinary service appointments, not stated to be exclusive, and they do not restrict us from engaging other providers: Section 7.2 gives us Servicer Termination Events and Section 7.4 expressly contemplates appointment of a Successor Servicer (including an unaffiliated institution whose regular business includes servicing receivables). This meets the preferred position of no exclusivity obligation on the customer, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-87883a3a","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"termination fee\", \"make-whole\" and \"forfeit\" return no provision imposing liquidated damages or a penalty on the Issuer or Depositor (our parties). This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, so no redline is warranted. The termination architecture in fact runs in our favour: on Servicer resignation or removal under Article VII there is no break fee, make-whole or minimum-fee payable by the Issuer to Cellco, Cellco must continue performing and assumes the Section 2.5/2.6 and Master Trust receivables-acquisition obligations (p0316, p0327), and Section 7.5(c) makes the resigning or terminated Servicer bear all reasonable transition expenses of the Issuer, the Trustees and the Successor Servicer (p0347). Section 8.3 termination is event-driven with no exit payment. Two items noted but not deviations: (i) the $150,000 appointment fee and Additional Successor Servicer Fee under Section 7.4(c) (p0339) are compensation for services rendered by a third-party replacement servicer paid out of Collections, not a liquidated amount owed to the counterparty; and (ii) Make-Whole Payments under Article VIII are noteholder prepayment economics arising only from a voluntary Optional Redemption elected by the Class A Certificateholder, not a penalty imposed on us by the Servicer/Marketing Agent. Marketing Agent and Servicer deposit/remittance shortfall mechanics in Articles IV and VI likewise impose payment obligations on the counterparty, which benefit our side and are not flagged.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-2a614953","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"The Agreement contains no licence grant in our favour: Article IX has no name/mark or systems-use licence, and the only licence-adjacent provision is Section 7.5(b) (p0346), which expressly relieves Cellco as Servicer of any obligation to provide, license or assign its servicing processes, models, software or applications to the Issuer or any Successor Servicer. That is an outright exclusion of the operational users the playbook protects — our affiliates and the Successor Servicer and contractors who would actually run servicing — with no path to add them, which sits in walk-away territory rather than at the fallback (affiliates on written notice, transferable to a successor). Section 7.5(a) cooperation on transition does not cure this, since cooperation confers no right to use the servicing platform. Our redline inserts a narrow non-exclusive licence extending to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, transferable to a subsequent Successor Servicer and revocable only for uncured material breach, limited to servicing the Receivables and expressly subject to the Servicer's legal and third-party restrictions, so the existing carve-outs for confidentiality, privacy and data protection are preserved. We did not flag the revocable power of attorney in Section 3.2(f) (p0105): that authority is granted by the Issuer to the Servicer and its revocability runs in our favour.","proposal":"Carve a limited, non-revocable servicing-platform licence out of the Servicer's blanket refusal to license its processes and software on transition","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-b4eb533b","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"The only limitation-of-liability language is the exculpation regime in Section 6.2(a) (counterparty) and Section 5.2(a) (our Depositor); there is no monetary cap anywhere, and the absence of a cap favours us as claimant, so we do not push a fees-based cap (a Servicing Fee-based cap would be illusory). The material failure is direction and mutuality: Section 6.2(a) makes Cellco liable \"only\" for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, whereas the mirror provision for the Depositor (p0243) omits \"only\". Coupled with the blanket waiver of \"All other liability\", the counterparty's exculpation is capable of excusing ordinary breach of its core performance obligations — the Servicer Deposit Obligation, the Servicer Acquisition Obligation and remittance of Collections — which are our principal recourse, i.e. an effectively zero-value, one-sided limitation in the counterparty's favour (walk-away territory under this rule). The Section 6.3 indemnities are likewise triggered only by willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence. The minimal edit deletes \"only\" to restore symmetry with Section 5.2(a) and states that the Servicer's/Marketing Agent's specific obligations and indemnities sit outside any limitation on liability, without importing a cap.","proposal":"Remove the one-sided \"only\" exculpation in Section 6.2(a) and confirm the Servicer's/Marketing Agent's specific obligations (deposit, acquisition and indemnity) sit outside any liability limitation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-400e0890","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX OTHER AGREEMENTS","rationale":"No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binds us. Searches for \"compete\"/\"competing\", \"exclusiv\", \"solicit\", and \"will not engage/develop/market/sell\" return no restrictive covenant, and a full read of Article IX (Other Agreements) and Article V (Depositor) shows only transaction-protective covenants: Section 9.2 bars the Depositor from transferring or encumbering the Depositor Transferred Property already sold to the Issuer, Section 5.6/5.7 are standard SPE existence and no-division covenants, and the Issuer's only activity limits are the self-imposed Permitted Activities in the Trust Agreement. The Section 9.9 ri[REDACTED] transfer/hedging restriction binds Cellco as Sponsor (the counterparty), and the Section 9.10 Cap Collateral Account covenant merely constrains the Issuer's exercise of control over collateral it holds for its own benefit. None of these limits the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, so the clause set meets the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-d96bd497","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"Counterparty side is better than our preferred position: Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer except where legally unable to perform, and Section 7.3 requires it to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement, so there is no Vendor termination-for-convenience right. However, on our side the only route to remove the Servicer is Section 7.2(c) for a Servicer Termination Event (i.e. for cause), and the Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3) — well beyond 12 months. The Optional Acquisition/Clean-Up Redemption (Section 8.1) and Optional Redemption (Section 8.2) are held by the Class A Certificateholder, defined as \"the Originators or their designee\" (counterparty-side), and require agreement on the Optional Acquisition Amount, so they are not a customer convenience exit. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months fails the fallback, so we have added a 30-day no-fee convenience termination right, conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement under Section 7.4 to preserve servicing continuity for the Noteholders.","proposal":"Add an Issuer right to terminate the Servicer for convenience on 30 days' notice, without fee, subject to Successor Servicer continuity","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-ce37bb37","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The direction of the audit/inspection rights in this agreement is inverted relative to the rule: every review right runs against the counterparty, not against us. Section 3.6 (p0131) gives the Issuer, Depositor and other transaction parties an annual, reasonable-notice review of the Servicer's (Cellco's) records at Cellco's offices, and Section 3.9(e) (p0146) gives the Depositor, Issuer and Indenture Trustee access to the Receivable Files and receivables systems held by Cellco as Custodian; the Regulation AB items (Compliance Statement, Servicing Assessment, Attestation Report and Annual Certification) are likewise deliverables of Cellco, at its cost. No provision grants Cellco or any other party an audit, inspection or verification right against the Issuer or the Depositor, and there is no obligation for us to bear audit costs or to grant access to our systems. Accordingly the rule's concerns (frequency, notice, cost, system access binding the customer) are not engaged, and these clauses benefit our party, so we do not redline them. Noted only for the record: the review right we hold is exercisable at the Servicer's offices and is subject to Cellco's security, confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies, which is customary for this deal type.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-0ce934fd","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"Section 10.5 makes the Agreement governed by the internal laws of the State of New York (and bars any amendment changing the governing law), and Section 10.6 submits the parties to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York and New York State courts sitting in New York, New York — the playbook's preferred New York law/New York County forum. Minor sub-element only: the jurisdiction grant is nonexclusive rather than exclusive, which is noted but not a material deviation and preserves our ability to sue elsewhere.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-1ef1f7e1","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"A-36","rationale":"Searches for MFN constructs (\"more favorable\", \"no less favorable\", \"most favored\", \"terms at least as\", \"offered to any other\") return no hits, and a full read of Article IX (Other Agreements) and Article X (Miscellaneous) — the only plausible locations for a covenant of this type — reveals no pricing or terms-matching covenant of any kind. The Servicer's compensation is a fixed Servicing Fee Rate of 0.75%, with no obligation on the Issuer or Depositor to extend to Cellco (as Servicer/Marketing Agent/Custodian) any better terms granted to a third party or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on our side), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-2e0fabb3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES","rationale":"The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on the Issuer or Depositor, so it sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; consideration is paid only for property actually transferred). The closest analogues all cut in our favour or are purely optional: (i) transfers of Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b)-(d) are conditional (Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests, Depositor certifications) and consideration equals the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount for receivables actually acquired — the Issuer is nowhere obliged to acquire a minimum volume; (ii) funding of the Acquisition Account and the related Negative Carry Account under Section 4.4(d)(i) and 4.4(c)(i) is made by the Class A Certificateholder \"solely at its option\", and Required Acquisition Deposit Amount / Required Negative Carry Amount are only internal cash-trapping levels with excesses released back to the Certificateholders, not payments we must make to the counterparty; (iii) the Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Article VIII are options, not obligations, and require full payment of the Notes; and (iv) the only \"shortfall\" mechanic (Section 4.3(h) Credit Payments) is an obligation of the Marketing Agent to fund us. The $425,000 Additional Successor Servicer Fee floor is a servicing-transition fee for a replacement servicer, not a purchase commitment, and it supports our ability to replace Cellco. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-8e67a3e7","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"Full-text searches for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"employ\" and \"induce\" return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant anywhere in the Agreement. Article VII (Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer), including the transition provisions in Sections 7.4 and 7.5, imposes only cooperation and records/funds-transfer duties on the outgoing Servicer, plus a carve-out preserving Cellco's proprietary processes and software; nothing restricts the Issuer, the Depositor, the Indenture Trustee or any Successor Servicer from soliciting or hiring Cellco servicing personnel on a Servicer transition. Article IX (Other Agreements) likewise contains no restrictive covenant of this kind. This meets the preferred position (no non-solicit binding our party), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-d64284b3","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","rationale":"This is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement with no subscription term, renewal term or evergreen mechanic. Article VIII fixes a single, self-liquidating term: the Agreement terminates automatically on the earlier of the last Receivable being paid in full/settled/sold/written off or termination of the Issuer under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement, with Sections 8.1 and 8.2 giving the Class A Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption exits. Searches for \"renew\", \"automatically renew\", \"successive\", \"extended for\" and \"unless either party gives notice\" return no results, so there is no automatic renewal, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price-uplift language. There is nothing to shorten or cap, and no exit risk to us as Issuer/Depositor (the Servicer cannot roll the term forward unilaterally). The auto-renewal rule is therefore inapplicable to this deal structure rather than breached; no redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-2322b8a4","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"A usable exit/transition regime exists and clears the fallback. Section 7.5 requires the outgoing Servicer to cooperate in an orderly transition (7.5(a)), to transfer all funds and to deliver the Receivable Files and the accounts and records it maintains to the Successor Servicer as soon as practicable after the effective date of resignation or termination (7.5(b)), and to bear all reasonable transition expenses of the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and Successor Servicer (7.5(c)) — i.e. transition assistance at the Servicer's cost rather than at its then-current rates, which is better than the preferred position for us. Section 7.3 requires Cellco to continue performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement (and to continue remittance obligations under 3.12(b) while any Receivable has a Principal Balance), so assistance runs well beyond 90 days/6 months. Section 3.10(f) separately requires the Custodian to deliver the Receivable Files to the Indenture Trustee or successor custodian on termination of its custodial appointment, again at the terminated custodian's expense. Walk-away territory (no data return, or immediate deletion) is not present. Minor sub-elements short of the model language, noted but not redlined: file/record delivery is \"as soon as practicable\" rather than a hard 30-day deadline; there is no deletion-and-certification mechanic (unsurprising here, since Cellco remains Marketing Agent/Administrator and needs Obligor data to bill the underlying accounts); and 7.5(b) carves out the Servicer's proprietary processes, models and servicing software and items restricted by confidentiality or privacy policies. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement (we act for the Issuer/Depositor side; Cellco acts as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian)

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Overall, the document is materially favourable to us. The counterparty-side indemnity in Section 6.3 is uncapped and there is no reverse indemnity from the Issuer or Depositor; the audit and inspection rights all run against Cellco rather than against us; and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment, auto-renewal or customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty anywhere in the document. Assignment is symmetric with appropriate successor and affiliate carve-outs, governing law and venue are New York, and the transition regime in Section 7.5 is better than our preferred position because the outgoing Servicer bears transition costs.

Four items require attention. Two are deviations that we regard as walk-away territory as drafted: (i) Section 7.5(b) expressly relieves Cellco of any obligation to license or assign its servicing processes, models, software or applications to the Issuer or a Successor Servicer, leaving us with no right to use the platform that actually runs servicing; and (ii) the Section 6.2(a) exculpation is one-sided — Cellco is liable "only" for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, while the mirror provision for our Depositor in Section 5.2(a) omits "only" — which is capable of excusing ordinary breach of the Servicer's core deposit, acquisition and remittance obligations. Separately, there is no customer termination-for-convenience right in an agreement that runs until the last Receivable is paid, and the Agreement contains no insurance covenant at all notwithstanding that Cellco holds Receivable Files and Personally Identifiable Information as Custodian.

One item, ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP), could not be completed by the automated review and requires manual attention before we sign off.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Section 6.3) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** | — (review incomplete) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Section 7.5(b)) |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | **Deviation** | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Section 6.2(a)) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Sections 7.1–7.3) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Section 10.2) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Sections 3.6, 3.9(e)) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Sections 10.5–10.6) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | A-36 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Transfer and Acquisition of Depositor Transferred Property |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § VIII Termination |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Section 7.5) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Sections 3.2, 3.3, 2.5) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § III Servicing of Receivables (no covenant in document) |

---

## Walk-away items

The following two findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signing:

1. **Servicing-platform licence (Section 7.5(b)).** The clause expressly relieves Cellco of any obligation to provide, license or assign its servicing processes, models, software or applications to the Issuer or any Successor Servicer, with no path to add our affiliates, contractors or a Successor Servicer. Section 7.5(a) cooperation does not cure this, because cooperation confers no right to use the platform. **Our redline** inserts a narrow non-exclusive licence extending to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, transferable to a subsequent Successor Servicer, revocable only for uncured material breach, limited to servicing the Receivables and expressly subject to the Servicer's legal and third-party restrictions so that the existing confidentiality, privacy and data protection carve-outs are preserved.

2. **One-sided exculpation (Section 6.2(a)).** Cellco is liable "only" for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence while the mirror provision for our Depositor at Section 5.2(a) omits "only", and the blanket waiver of "All other liability" is capable of excusing ordinary breach of the Servicer Deposit Obligation, the Servicer Acquisition Obligation and remittance of Collections — our principal recourse. The Section 6.3 indemnities are triggered by the same narrow standard. **Our redline** is minimal: delete "only" to restore symmetry with Section 5.2(a) and confirm that the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's specific obligations (deposit, acquisition and indemnity) sit outside any limitation on liability. We are not seeking a monetary cap — there is none today, and the absence of a cap favours us as claimant; a Servicing Fee-based cap would be illusory.

---

## Next steps

1. **Complete the IP review.** The ownership of deliverables and Customer Data analysis failed in processing and must be completed manually before we clear the document. This is a critical-severity rule and we should not sign off without it.
2. **Issue the two walk-away redlines** described above (Sections 7.5(b) and 6.2(a)) as priority items, with the rationale and fallback framing set out in each comment.
3. **Add a customer convenience exit.** There is no Issuer right to remove the Servicer other than for a Servicer Termination Event under Section 7.2(c), and the Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.3 — well beyond 12 months. The Article VIII optional acquisition and redemption rights sit with the Class A Certificateholder (the Originators or their designee), so they are not a customer exit. We propose a 30-day, no-fee convenience termination right, conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement under Section 7.4 to preserve servicing continuity for the Noteholders. Note the counterparty side is already better than our preferred position: Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning except where legally unable to perform.
4. **Insert an insurance covenant.** We propose a new Section 10.14 in Article X requiring Cellco, in all three of its capacities, to carry CGL (USD 1M/2M), E&O (USD 2M), cyber (USD 5M) and workers' compensation as required by law, with certificates on request, given that Cellco holds and maintains the Receivable Files and Personally Identifiable Information as Custodian and Exhibit A (Custodian's Security Requirements) is not reproduced in this form. Insurance covenants are atypical in a transfer and servicing agreement of this type and Section 6.3 provides some overlapping protection, so this is a low-severity ask; the fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if the full programme is resisted.
5. **Low-priority comment only.** Under Section 7.5(b), file and record delivery is "as soon as practicable" rather than subject to a hard outside date; we would raise a 30-day delivery deadline as a non-blocking comment. We also note, without redlining, that the Section 10.6 jurisdiction grant is nonexclusive (which preserves our ability to sue elsewhere) and that Section 6.3 has no IP-infringement limb (immaterial here, as there are no vendor deliverables or IP grant).
6. **Confirm Exhibit A.** Request the Custodian's Security Requirements exhibit, which is not reproduced in the form we reviewed, and review it against the insurance and data-handling positions above."}
